lines.trans: The three essentials for humans are clothing, food, and shelter, and once you enter the editing room you give up clothing and shelter.
The single thing left is food!
And if even that meal fails, all the fury naturally lands squarely on the youngest producer who ordered it.
That seems spot on—I got chewed out badly just earlier.
First off, checking their menu picks well before they get hungry is crucial.
Once a person starts getting hungry, anger settles right in as their baseline mood!
Second, never put forward the dish that you want to eat yourself!
Order out of laziness from a place with a hundred dishes and it will taste awful—always order from a specialty spot!
How do you tell whether someone has a kid's palate?
Just watch when they order coffee—some people order drinks with super long names.
Then it is one hundred percent—one hundred percent a kid's palate!

examples.text: 얘 지금 살려고 발버둥 치는 거 안 보여? 이런 거 보면 인간이 진짜 제일 잔인해.
examples.trans: Do you not see it struggling to stay alive right now? Seeing things like this, humans really are the cruelest.
Here the word for 'humans' is key.

examples.text: 여기가 바로 편집실이다, 앞으로 네가 가장 많은 밤을 새우게 될 곳이지.
examples.trans: This right here is the editing room—the place where you will pull the most all-nighters from now on.
Here the word for 'the most' is key.

meanings.note: Korean expresses 'need' as an adjective ('is needed by me').

examples.trans: I need help.
I need time.

examples.text: 수습 기간 중에 세 번 사고 치면 잘릴 수도 있대요.
examples.trans: I heard that if you cause trouble three times during probation, you can get fired.
The topic of three came up during this shoot.

examples.text: 정권 바뀌면 바꿀 게 한두 가지가 아니에요.
examples.trans: When leadership changes, there is way more than one or two things you have to change.
Here the word for 'kinds, items' is key.

examples.text: 인간한테 가장 필요한 세 가지가 의식주인데, 편집실에 들어가면 의랑 주는 포기해야 된단 말이에요.
examples.trans: The three essentials for humans are clothing, food, and shelter, and once you enter the editing room you give up clothing and shelter.

examples.text: 여기가 바로 편집실이다, 앞으로 네가 가장 많은 밤을 새우게 될 곳이지.

examples.text: 인간한테 가장 필요한 세 가지가 의식주인데, 편집실에 들어가면 의랑 주는 포기해야 된단 말이에요.
examples.trans: The three essentials for humans are clothing, food, and shelter, and once you enter the editing room you give up clothing and shelter.

meanings.note: Used in 이번 주 (this week), 다음 주 (next week)

examples.trans: One week is seven days.
I'm going to go on a trip next week.

examples.text: 인간한테 가장 필요한 세 가지가 의식주인데, 편집실에 들어가면 의랑 주는 포기해야 된단 말이에요.
examples.trans: The three essentials for humans are clothing, food, and shelter, and once you enter the editing room you give up clothing and shelter.
This expression comes from 'must give up'.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.
The single thing left is food!
Here the word for 'solely, only' is key.

meanings.note: Native Korean numeral; shortens to 한 before a counter noun (한 개, 한 명).

examples.trans: One coffee, please.
How much is one?
Money is left.
Time is left.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

examples.text: 나도 그런 식의 별명이 생겼으면 좋겠다는 거지.
examples.trans: So I hope I get a nickname like that too.

examples.text: 나한테 꼬인 걸 이런 식으로 풀면 안 되지.
examples.trans: You shouldn't take your frustration with me out on her like this.

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.
Mission failed!
Here the word for 'failure!' is key.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

examples.text: 이 식에서마저 실패를 하면 그 분노가 메뉴를 시킨 막내한테 오기 마련이죠.
examples.trans: And if even that meal fails, all the fury naturally lands squarely on the youngest producer who ordered it.
Here the word for 'anger, fury' is key.

examples.text: 이 식에서마저 실패를 하면 그 분노가 메뉴를 시킨 막내한테 오기 마련이죠.
examples.trans: And if even that meal fails, all the fury naturally lands squarely on the youngest producer who ordered it.
Here the word for 'the menu' is key.

meanings.en: to make someone do, to assign work
meanings.note: Causative verb; e.g., 일을 시키다 'to assign work'.
E.g., 치킨을 시키다 'to order fried chicken'.

examples.trans: The team leader assigned this work to me.
Shall we order pizza for dinner?
Did you hear about this youngest member?
I was busy today because of youngest member.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

examples.text: 이 식에서마저 실패를 하면 그 분노가 메뉴를 시킨 막내한테 오기 마련이죠.
examples.trans: And if even that meal fails, all the fury naturally lands squarely on the youngest producer who ordered it.
Here the word for 'is bound to happen' is key.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.en: earlier, a short while ago (same day)

examples.trans: I called earlier.
What did you say earlier?

examples.text: 그런 것 같습니다, 아까 야단 엄청 맞았습니다.
examples.trans: That seems spot on—I got chewed out badly just earlier.
Here the word for 'scolding' is key.
The weather is super cold today.
That movie was super fun.

맞다.gloss: to be right, to be correct

meanings.note: Used to confirm facts or answers.

meanings.en: to fit, to suit, to match

examples.trans: Yes, that's my phone number.
These shoes fit my feet perfectly.

meanings.en: first of all, for starters, for the time being
meanings.note: marks an immediate first step before dealing with anything else

examples.trans: Let's sit down and talk first.
Let's wait until today for now.

examples.text: 일단은 배가 고프기 전에 미리미리 메뉴 체크를 하는 게 중요해요.
examples.trans: First off, checking their menu picks well before they get hungry is crucial.
Here the word for 'stomach' is key.

examples.text: 일단은 배가 고프기 전에 미리미리 메뉴 체크를 하는 게 중요해요.
examples.trans: First off, checking their menu picks well before they get hungry is crucial.

examples.text: 나 마음 바뀌기 전에 빨리 계약서 보내는 게 좋을 거예요.
examples.trans: You had better send the contract quickly before I change my mind.

examples.text: 게임을 하기 전에 미리 확인을 받으라고? 지금 장난해?
examples.trans: Get approval in advance before every game? Are you kidding me right now?

examples.text: 일단은 배가 고프기 전에 미리미리 메뉴 체크를 하는 게 중요해요.
examples.trans: First off, checking their menu picks well before they get hungry is crucial.
Here the word for 'well in advance' is key.

examples.text: 일단은 배가 고프기 전에 미리미리 메뉴 체크를 하는 게 중요해요.
examples.trans: First off, checking their menu picks well before they get hungry is crucial.
Here the word for 'check' is key.
Health is the most important thing.
There is an important meeting today.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.
The meeting is starting soon.
I started studying Korean.

meanings.note: Denotes a fundamental rule or baseline expectation. With the copula 이다, 기본이다 means 'is basic/standard'. RR: gibon.

examples.trans: Greeting others is basic in workplace life.
Being on time is standard, right?

examples.text: 사람이 배가 고프기 시작하면 기본 베이스에 화가 깔린다!
examples.trans: Once a person starts getting hungry, anger settles right in as their baseline mood!
Here the word for 'at the baseline' is key.
A saint never loses her temper, though.
The topic of anger came up during this shoot.

examples.text: 사람이 배가 고프기 시작하면 기본 베이스에 화가 깔린다!
examples.trans: Once a person starts getting hungry, anger settles right in as their baseline mood!
This expression comes from 'underlies, settles in!'.
I bought bread. And I bought milk too.
Let's eat and then depart.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for eating a meal or food; honorific equivalent is 드시다.

examples.trans: Let's eat lunch together.
Did you eat breakfast?

meanings.note: Auxiliary adjective attached to a verb stem with -고 (-고 싶다).

examples.trans: I want to go to Korea.
I want to drink a cup of coffee.

examples.text: 그리고 내가 먹고 싶은 메뉴를 앞세우지 않는다!
examples.trans: Second, never put forward the dish that you want to eat yourself!
This expression comes from 'push to the front'.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.en: to be bothersome, annoying, a hassle
meanings.note: Describes something troublesome or too much effort to deal with.

examples.trans: Cooking is a hassle.
It's a hassle if there are lots of people.

examples.text: 귀찮다고 메뉴 100가지 있는 집에서 시켰다간 맛없어, 음식은 전문점에서!
examples.trans: Order out of laziness from a place with a hundred dishes and it will taste awful—always order from a specialty spot!
Here the word for 'a hundred kinds' is key.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)

meanings.note: Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.trans: I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.

examples.text: 귀찮다고 메뉴 100가지 있는 집에서 시켰다간 맛없어, 음식은 전문점에서!
examples.trans: Order out of laziness from a place with a hundred dishes and it will taste awful—always order from a specialty spot!
This expression comes from 'tastes bad'.

examples.text: 귀찮다고 메뉴 100가지 있는 집에서 시켰다간 맛없어, 음식은 전문점에서!
examples.trans: Order out of laziness from a place with a hundred dishes and it will taste awful—always order from a specialty spot!

Here the word for 'child, kid' is key.

Here the word for 'having a palate' is key.

How should we solve this problem?

examples.text: 커피 시킬 때 보면 돼요, 이름 긴 거 시키는 사람들 있거든.
examples.trans: Just watch when they order coffee—some people order drinks with super long names.
Here the word for 'coffee' is key.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
Please write your name here.
What is that puppy's name?

examples.text: 커피 시킬 때 보면 돼요, 이름 긴 거 시키는 사람들 있거든.
examples.trans: Just watch when they order coffee—some people order drinks with super long names.
This expression comes from 'long'.
Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!
Then it is one hundred percent—one hundred percent a kid's palate!
Here the word for 'is one hundred percent' is key.
